prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

statement.case_for: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is the case on the shortlist where a simple, analytically transparent model (the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model of 2011) made a sharp, non-obvious prediction, and an experiment seven years later found the predicted physics together with unexpected correlated insulators and superconductivity. The mechanism is understood at the level of the essential model, not just observed, which is the question I always ask of a breakthrough. It has also spawned a broad field (moire quantum matter, twistronics) that has been reproduced in many laboratories and extended to other moire platforms. Having read the other opening ballots, I note that B001 was ranked in the top eight by seven members and in the top three by six, so the support is broad, though I do not equate that with merit. The theory-plus-experiment structure maps naturally to three names.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that the field is still young and the pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unsettled, so one could argue the prize should wait. There is also a real attribution problem: earlier continuum-type work on twisted bilayers (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto), the first-author students of the 2018 papers, and contemporaneous experimental groups (for example Dean, Watanabe, Taniguchi) are not covered by the three-name limit, so the configuration will look contestable to the physics community. If the committee judges that the discovery is not yet settled enough, the optical lattice clock (B007) is the more mature and less contested choice.

responses.point: Ulf ranks the optical lattice clock first as a mature, instrument-level discovery with clean two-person attribution, and ranks twisted bilayer graphene second, noting it is quite mature for its age but slightly early because the pairing mechanism is unresolved.
responses.response: I agree that B007 has the cleaner attribution and the longer track record, and I do not dismiss it; it is my first alternative. But I do not think an unresolved pairing mechanism is a maturity problem for the prize criterion. The discovery being rewarded is the flat-band prediction and the existence of correlated and superconducting states in a tunable platform, and both are firmly reproduced. Pairing in cuprates has been unresolved for decades and nobody argues the discovery was premature. Where I do take his point seriously is that B001's credit list is more fragile than the clock's, and I would not want us to hide that behind enthusiasm for the physics.

responses.point: Olle puts twisted bilayer graphene first and topological insulators second, valuing the surprise-in-a-material character and the direct theory-experiment loop, and he flags the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang credit gap in B023.
responses.response: I agree with him on B001, and on why the theory-experiment loop is unusually direct here. On B023 I share his worry: Kane-Mele is clean, but the HgTe experiment followed the BHZ prediction, and a prize crediting Kane, Mele and Molenkamp without Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang would be hard to defend scientifically. That is why I keep B023 only as a second alternative and do not put it in my preferred configuration. It is also overlapping in spirit with the 2016 topological-phase prize, which weakens the novelty argument relative to moire physics.

responses.point: Mark ranks IceCube first as the most convincing instrument-driven discovery, while conceding the very large collaboration makes any two or three names a simplification and that KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD are still maturing; he ranks twisted bilayer graphene third and says condensed matter is outside his expertise.
responses.response: I respect the instrument argument, and the neutrino detection is real. My reservation is attribution: an honest credit for IceCube is to a collaboration of hundreds, and the three credited names do not capture who first decided that a cubic kilometre was the right size or who made the analyses work. I would rather reward a discovery where the credited individuals clearly stand for the decisive idea and experiment. Since he leans on colleagues for condensed matter, I would note for the record that the reproduction of correlated phases across many independent groups is the kind of independent confirmation his instrument case also relies on.

responses.point: Eva ranks aberration-corrected electron microscopy first for its overdue, fully mature impact on materials physics, and puts twisted bilayer graphene second with timing described as early but defensible.
responses.response: I agree that B030 is a genuine invention and clearly mature, and on timing I accept her phrase, early but defensible, as a fair description of B001. My difference is about what the prize is for: the corrector is an enabling tool, and the 1986 prize already recognised the electron microscope itself, whereas B001 is a discovery of new physics. I would not rule out B030 on merit, but I would want the committee to say explicitly why a tool should rank above a new phase of matter here.

uncertainties: Whether the three-name limit can be applied to B001 without an unfair omission of earlier twisted-bilayer theory or the first-author experimenters.
Whether the unresolved origin of the superconductivity will be read by the wider committee as a maturity problem.
I have not independently verified the detailed priority claims for earlier continuum-model theory, which rest on memory of the literature.
Whether the committee prefers a single moire prize or would pair it with a second achievement such as B007, which would force a reduction in credited names.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. I have no collaboration with any credited candidate on the shortlist. Goran Johansson and Eva Olsson are in the closely linked Chalmers physics environment, but I have no specific collaboration with them that would require recusal.
